headline.text: The FDA label reports increased tizanidine exposure and adverse reactions with alcohol.

reported.text: A case report describes syncope from postural hypotension after concurrent ingestion.

claims.text: The FDA label says alcohol increases tizanidine exposure, associated with increased adverse reactions.
claims.quote:
Alcohol increases the exposure of tizanidine after administration of tizanidine.
This was associated with an increase in adverse reactions of tizanidine.
claims.judgeRationale: The tizanidine label states alcohol increases tizanidine exposure and this was associated with more adverse reactions.

claims.text: A case report describes postural hypotension and syncope in a 53-year-old woman after concurrent tizanidine and alcohol ingestion.
claims.quote: We present a case of a 53-year-old female with alcohol use disorder who presented with a first-time syncopal attack due to postural hypotension after ingesting both tizanidine and alcohol concurrently.
claims.judgeRationale: The claim presents the abstract as a single case report of syncope from postural hypotension, matching the quote.

sources.title: Syncope Secondary to Concomitant Ingestion of Tizanidine and Alcohol in a Patient With Alcohol Use Disorder.
Tizanidine distribution in a postmortem case.
sources.citation: 0146-4760 30 5 2006 Jun Journal of analytical toxicology J Anal Toxicol

pharmacistQuestions.text: The evidence here is limited. Is there anything about my health that makes this interaction more or less relevant?
Do any of my other medicines or products, like cough syrup or mouthwash, contain alcohol?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Tizanidine and drinking alcohol, change how much this matters?

gaps.text: The packet contains no controlled human interaction study; a case report cannot quantify incidence.
